source_or_gap: The book already separated learning, evaluation, evidence, readiness, repair, and operations, but lacked one explicit competence-dependent allocation hypothesis joining positive-support saturation, evaluator limits, informative exceptions, least-invasive repairs, useful-coverage floors, and recovery under equal-total-cost accounting.
chapter_action_policy: Integrate only each owner's distinct responsibility: regime allocation, bounded feedback, exception custody, evaluator-first repair, saturation diagnosis, field qualification, readiness separation, procedural compilation, incident clocks, joined lifecycle, scoped evidence semantics, artifact lineage, or equal-total-cost accounting. Do not create a paper-shaped chapter.
merge_or_split_policy: Keep the manuscript as one public author-paper record and distribute its bounded concepts across established owners. Reconsider a new chapter only if a later implementation reveals a durable service lifecycle that cannot be governed through those interfaces.
boundary_decision_rationale: GRBL is a cross-layer learning-and-assurance lifecycle, not a new authority domain. Learning topology allocates work; evaluators discover and judge; data and procedural memory retain and compile; capability fields own repair scope; readiness owns admission; operations owns containment and recovery; evidence and artifact owners preserve claims and lineage.
external_literature_need: review every cited external source at full-paper depth before using its results as book evidence
